page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs based on the Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, with 24 physical cores and a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.r7.6xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1843.79 and a multi-core score of 23250.96. Memory bandwidth tests show 1263.88 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 129.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 11538.47 and handles 23.5 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. For language model workloads, it demonstrates strong text generation performance of 283.7 tokens per second on a small 135M model, though performance scales down to 14.18 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density make this instance suitable for memory-bound enterprise workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. However, the lack of local NVMe storage means all disk I/O must traverse the 12 Gbps network interface, which may limit performance for I/O-heavy databases. The ecs.r7.6xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive applications, including in-memory databases like Redis, medium-scale database operations, software compilation, and caching layers.
